title: Small scalp field errors can give large electrode errors in a skull model
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) measures voltage at electrodes on the scalp. We tested errors from a simple electrical skull model. A complete scalp field test can miss errors at a finite electrode array. We calculated fields in concentric tissue layers. We used a public 64-electrode layout and published conductivity data. The main source pattern had 0.3484% error over the complete scalp. Its mean-referenced electrode voltage was zero within numerical precision. A small added source gave 151.8% relative electrode error. The absolute error was 0.1518% of the largest output for a unit source. We give a sharp error bound with an explicit source penalty. We checked 252 assigned heads and two skull reductions. A separate interface solver agreed within 7.2e-14 relative error. These results apply to fixed spherical heads and specified sources. They do not give error rates for people.

display.caption: Modal skull errors, sharp bounds with an explicit source penalty, near-silent source sequences, and 252 assigned heads. All electrode outputs are mean referenced. The source penalty is not a noise level.
A smooth radial source pattern, reference scalp field and reduction error. Electrode directions are black points. Each panel has its own scale; the source is silent only after the sensor reference.
